text: The family here is read from a conditional sentence: "All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset" describes the ones that use that silicon rather than claiming the range does. This record is the brand's catch-all, so it asserts the chip for every iFi converter on evidence that does not go that far.
resolution: The per-input ceilings were WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24, on the claim's own confession: its source ended with « This record is the range's catch-all and the figures are the Pro iDSD's; the Neo and micro models were not documented per input. » A source that says it does not cover the subject is evidence against the claim it carries.
evidence_kept: iFi Pro iDSD manual, read 2026-11-20, which states it plainly: « Inputs other than USB are currently limited to maximum sample rates of 192kHz PCM and DSD64 via DoP », against USB at 768 kHz and DSD1024.
what_would_resolve_it: A per-model record (ifi/pro-idsd) carrying them. The quoted sentence is unusually clean evidence and should not be lost on the way.
device_level_resolution: The DEVICE-level ceilings went the same way as the per-input ones, and for a reason that needs no judgement: this claim's quoted source carries NO figure at all - it reads « All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset » and « TI/BB DAC chips only support bit-perfect DSD playback ». It supports a chip family and a DSD behaviour, and nothing about a rate. The figures it was carrying (768 kHz, DSD512) were the Pro iDSD's, as the withdrawn per-input claim said in its own words. Withdrawing the per-input ceilings and keeping the device-level ones would have left the record LOOKING reviewed while still asserting one model's rates for the range.
device_level_kept: family, dsd_direct, analog_filter and correctable stay: the quote reaches the chip and its DSD behaviour, which is exactly what it talks about.
